claims.text: The target component is an Inconel 718 component previously subjected to fusion-welding repair and exhibiting hot cracking and a coarse, inhomogeneous microstructure.
Friction stir processing can repair or improve the damaged surface of an Inconel 718 component.
FSP uses a non-consumable tool plunged into or applied to the surface.
A rotation rate of 800–1200 rpm is an appropriate processing range for FSP of the Inconel 718 surface.
The proposed FSP can be performed under ambient conditions without shielding gas.
FSP is a solid-state thermomechanical process conducted below the melting temperature.
Plastic deformation during FSP can produce an ultrafine or nanostructured surface layer.
Mechanical stirring and severe plastic deformation during FSP induce dynamic recrystallization and grain refinement in Inconel 718.
FSP homogenizes the grains and microstructure of the processed Inconel 718 layer.
FSP induces beneficial compressive residual stresses in the processed surface.
Grain refinement and compressive residual stresses delay the initiation and propagation of hot cracks.
The FSP-treated surface will have higher hardness than both a fusion-welded repair and an untreated surface.
The FSP-treated surface will have greater wear resistance than both a fusion-welded repair and an untreated surface.
The FSP-treated surface will have greater corrosion resistance than both a fusion-welded repair and an untreated surface.
The FSP-treated surface will delay hot-cracking onset relative to both a fusion-welded repair and an untreated surface.
The proposed benefits will persist under high temperatures, corrosive media, mechanical wear, and thermal cycling typical of nickel-superalloy service.
The proposed experiment compares FSP-treated, fusion-welded, and untreated Inconel 718 panels under common thermal, corrosion, and wear exposures.
Failure to obtain statistically significant property improvements or a delay in hot-cracking initiation relative to both controls is designated as a falsifying outcome.

contradictions.description: The intervention is applied to a surface stated to already exhibit hot cracks, while the predicted outcome and experiment focus on delaying crack initiation or onset. Existing cracks cannot have their initiation delayed unless they are first removed or healed, but no such step is specified.
